speaker: dvm
text: Hi, it's Doctor Okafor calling from the clinic. I have Pepper here for her glucose curve. Do you have a few minutes?

speaker: client
text: Yes, of course. How is she doing?

speaker: dvm
text: She's doing well. Before I go through the numbers, can you tell me how much insulin you've been giving her at home?

speaker: client
text: Two units of the glargine, twice a day. Morning at seven and evening at seven, right after she eats.

speaker: dvm
text: And is she still drinking a lot of water?

speaker: client
text: Less than before. I used to fill her bowl three times a day, and now it's about once a day.

speaker: dvm
text: That's a good sign. How about her appetite and the litter box?

speaker: client
text: She's eating well. The clumps in the litter are smaller now. But she threw up once on Saturday, just a hairball I think.

speaker: dvm
text: Any wobbliness, weakness, or times she seemed sleepy or out of it, especially in the afternoon?

speaker: client
text: No, nothing like that. She's been jumping up on the counter again, which she hadn't done in months.

speaker: dvm
text: Great. Has she missed any doses?

speaker: client
text: One on Thursday night. She didn't finish her dinner, so I skipped it like you told me.

speaker: dvm
text: That was the right thing to do. Okay, here are her numbers today. She weighs four point eight kilos, up from four point five last month.

speaker: dvm
text: Her glucose this morning before insulin was three hundred and ten. The lowest point was one hundred and sixty, at about six hours. That's called the nadir.

speaker: dvm
text: Her fructosamine came back at four hundred and eighty, which is still a little high.

speaker: client
text: So is that good or bad?

speaker: dvm
text: It's better, but she's not fully regulated yet. I'd like to increase her insulin to two and a half units twice a day.

speaker: client
text: Okay, two and a half units. Can I measure a half unit with the syringes I have?

speaker: client
text: They're the one hundred unit syringes, the half milliliter ones.

speaker: dvm
text: Those have half unit markings, so yes. We'll show you at pickup.

speaker: dvm
text: If she ever seems weak, wobbly, or has a seizure, rub some corn syrup on her gums and call us right away, or the emergency hospital if we're closed.

speaker: client
text: Corn syrup on the gums. Got it.

speaker: dvm
text: I'd like to repeat the glucose curve in two weeks. Keep her on the same diabetic food.

speaker: client
text: She's on the dry diabetic food, and I give her a spoon of the canned one at night. Is that okay?

speaker: dvm
text: Yes, as long as it's the same amount every night. She can go home at four o'clock.

speaker: client
text: Perfect. I'll be there at four. Thank you, Doctor.
